name: vision.ocr
description: Extract text and per-line bounding boxes from a region, window, monitor, image file, or supplied byte buffer. Token-cheap alternative to screen.capture for text-heavy UIs (60-250x context reduction). If no source selector is supplied, OCRs the entire virtual screen.

region.description: Rectangle in virtual-screen coordinates. Mutually exclusive with the other selectors.

window.description: Window handle, e.g. 'win:0x1A2B'. Mutually exclusive with the other selectors.

monitor.description: Zero-based monitor index per `system.info.screens`. Mutually exclusive with the other selectors.

path.description: Absolute path to an image file. Codec sniffed from magic bytes; supported set is `system.info.capabilities.ocr_input_formats`. Mutually exclusive with the other selectors.

bytes.description: Raw image bytes. Base64-encoded in tool-call form; bridges may transport as a length-prefixed wire payload (same convention as `file.write` / `clipboard.set`). Mutually exclusive with the other selectors.

bytes_format.description: Codec of the supplied `bytes`. Required when `bytes` is present; ignored otherwise.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag (e.g. "en-US", "ja"). Defaults to the OS user's preferred OCR language. Returns `not_supported` with `available_languages` detail if the requested pack isn't installed.

min_confidence.description: Drop lines whose engine-reported confidence is below this threshold from both `lines` and the joined `text`. Engines that don't report per-line confidence treat every line as 1.0 (always retained).

include_word_bboxes.description: If true, each line in the response gains a `words` array with per-word `text`, `bbox`, and `confidence`. Default false keeps the typical-case payload tight; opt in when word-level click-targeting is needed.

x-conditional.description: bytes_format is required when bytes is supplied — the agent has no other way to identify the codec.

text.description: Full extracted text, lines joined by `\n`. Reflects `min_confidence` filtering — lines below the threshold are absent here AND from `lines`.

bbox.description: Line's position and size, in `coordinate_space` units.

confidence.description: Engine-reported confidence, 0.0–1.0. Per-word values from `Windows.Media.Ocr` are averaged into per-line. Absent on engines that don't report it; treat absence as 1.0 for filtering purposes.

bbox.description: Word's position and size, in `coordinate_space` units.

words.description: Per-word entries. Present iff `include_word_bboxes: true` was supplied.

lines.description: Per-line entries in the engine's reading order (top-to-bottom for Latin scripts; engine-dependent for vertical / RTL).

language_used.description: BCP-47 tag the engine actually used. Equals `language` when supplied; otherwise the OS user-profile default the engine selected.

coordinate_space.description: Coordinate system for every `bbox` in the response. `screen` for region/window/monitor sources (virtual-screen coordinates). `image` for path/bytes sources (the source image's pixel grid). Always set; lets callers interpret bboxes unambiguously regardless of source.

image_size.description: Dimensions of the buffer OCR ran on. For region/window/monitor sources: the post-clamp captured rectangle (in virtual-screen coords; `x`/`y` are the top-left). For path/bytes sources: the source image's full extent (in image coords; `x`/`y` are 0).

text_angle.description: Degrees clockwise from horizontal that the engine detected the text rotated by, from `OcrResult.TextAngle`. 0.0 for upright content. Useful for rotated scans / vertical-script content.

x-implementations.name: windows_media_ocr
x-implementations.description: For live sources (region/window/monitor): captures pixels via the same path as `screen.capture` (WGC → BitBlt fallback) into a SoftwareBitmap. For static sources (path/bytes): decodes via `BitmapDecoder.CreateAsync` from a file stream or in-memory buffer; codec sniffed from magic bytes (path) or supplied via `bytes_format` (bytes). The SoftwareBitmap is then passed to `OcrEngine.RecognizeAsync`. Per-line `BoundingRect` from `OcrLine` populates `bbox`; per-word `Confidence` averaged into per-line `confidence`.

windows-modern.description: `Windows.Media.Ocr.OcrEngine` on Win 10 1803+ — the same OS-version cliff as WGC capture, so any agent that supports `screen.capture`'s fast path also supports OCR. Language packs are user-installed (Settings → Time & Language → Language → [language] → Options → OCR); the agent advertises installed packs via `system.info.capabilities.ocr_languages` (BCP-47 array, populated from `OcrEngine.AvailableRecognizerLanguages` at startup). Empty array means the verb is advertised but every call returns `ERR not_supported` until a pack is installed (or `OcrEngine.TryCreateFromUserProfileLanguages()` returned null because no language profile is configured). The engine's `MaxImageDimension` is advertised via `system.info.capabilities.ocr_max_dimension`; oversize sources return `ERR image_too_large` with `{max_dimension, observed: {w, h}}` detail. Supported decoder formats are advertised via `system.info.capabilities.ocr_input_formats`; unrecognised codecs (sniffed for `path`, declared for `bytes`) return `ERR unsupported_format` with `{format, supported_formats}` detail. Future tesseract integration on this family would graduate to a multi-implementation chain; the wire surface stays unchanged.

windows-classic.reason: No built-in OCR API on classic-stack Windows. Future agent builds may bundle tesseract; until then `vision.ocr` is omitted from this family's `system.capabilities` and from `dist/verbs-windows-classic.md`. Plugin-supplied OCR could fill this gap once the caller-side plugin runtime ships, but plugins can't shadow native verb names — a plugin-supplied vision engine on classic would expose a different verb (e.g. `vision.ocr_tesseract`).
